research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic research-source confidence only: direct official CAA, GOV.UK/MOD, HSE and Planning Data verification; 2026 currentness where available; aviation safeguarding/OLS/IFP/CNS, PSZ, hazardous-substances consent/COMAH, major-accident-hazard pipeline consultation zones, explosives separation-distance/safeguarding-plan and NO_DATA provenance gates. Not parcel-level accuracy.

verification.method: Direct official-web verification plus repository duplicate searches

official_sources.name: CAA What is safeguarding?
official_sources.fact: CAA explains officially safeguarded aerodromes, safeguarding maps, consultation triggers, wildlife circles and renewable-energy safeguarding.
official_sources.gate: Safeguarding consultation or a map trigger is not planning refusal, exact obstacle infringement or proof that mitigation cannot resolve the issue.

official_sources.name: CAA Planning consultations
official_sources.fact: CAA states aerodrome safeguarding responsibility for developments at or near aerodromes rests with the aerodrome operator, with separate guidance for cranes and other obstacles.
official_sources.gate: A CAA planning-consultation page is not an aerodrome decision, planning decision or site-specific clearance.

official_sources.name: CAA Safeguarding FAQ
official_sources.fact: CAA guidance covers officially safeguarded aerodromes, wind turbines, solar PV, CNS, glint/glare and related mitigation questions.
official_sources.gate: Potential aviation impact is not a parcel prohibition; exact aerodrome, protected surfaces, proposal geometry and mitigation must be assessed.

official_sources.name: CAP 738 Safeguarding of Aerodromes
official_sources.fact: CAP 738 is listed by CAA as current guidance for assessing effects of development or construction on aerodrome or technical-site operations.
official_sources.gate: Current guidance does not prove an exact proposal infringes OLS, CNS or IFP criteria.

official_sources.name: CAA Safeguarding of IFP
official_sources.fact: CAA requires separate safeguarding assessment of proposed development and temporary obstacles against current and possible future instrument flight procedures.
official_sources.gate: Need for IFP assessment is not an adverse finding; exact APDO assessment evidence is required.

official_sources.name: CAA safeguarding publications
official_sources.fact: CAA lists current safeguarding circulars, legislation and CAP publications used for aerodrome and technical-site safeguarding.
official_sources.gate: A publication index is provenance evidence, not parcel-specific safeguarding status.

official_sources.name: CAP 764 Wind Turbines
official_sources.fact: CAA lists CAP 764 edition 7, dated 17 December 2025, as current policy and guidance on wind turbines and aviation effects.
official_sources.gate: Wind-development aviation guidance does not prove radar, OLS, IFP or airspace impact for a specific turbine without assessment.

official_sources.name: CAA Windfarms
official_sources.fact: CAA states potential negative aviation impacts from wind turbines must be considered case by case and points to CAP 764.
official_sources.gate: A generic aviation concern must not be promoted to automatic refusal or exact-site incompatibility.

official_sources.name: CAP1096 crane guidance
official_sources.fact: CAP1096 provides current guidance on crane notification plus obstacle lighting and marking.
official_sources.gate: Crane guidance or notification is not an aerodrome permit, planning permission or safe-height determination for an exact crane.

official_sources.name: CAA crane notification
official_sources.fact: CAA states mandatory notification applies to cranes at or above 100m AGL and provides current crane-notification procedures.
official_sources.gate: Notification does not establish planning acceptability, aerodrome clearance or absence of local safeguarding requirements.

official_sources.name: CAP 772 Wildlife Hazard Management
official_sources.fact: CAA lists CAP 772 as current guidance on bird and wildlife hazard management at aerodromes and surrounding land.
official_sources.gate: A land use that may attract birds requires site-specific assessment; proximity alone is not proof of unacceptable bird-strike risk.

official_sources.name: CAP 736 lights and fireworks
official_sources.fact: CAA lists CAP 736 as current guidance for directed lights, fireworks, toy balloons and sky lanterns affecting UK airspace.
official_sources.gate: Notification or airspace guidance is not planning permission or a permanent parcel constraint.

official_sources.name: CAA outdoor lasers and fireworks
official_sources.fact: CAA provides current notification guidance for outdoor lasers, searchlights, fireworks, pyrotechnics and sky lanterns.
official_sources.gate: Temporary event notification requirements must not be converted into permanent development constraints.

official_sources.name: Safeguarded aerodromes direction 2002
official_sources.fact: The government direction establishes consultation arrangements for safeguarded aerodromes, technical sites and military explosives storage areas, including separate wind-turbine maps.
official_sources.gate: A statutory consultation direction is not a parcel-level objection or refusal and requires the exact safeguarding map criteria.

official_sources.name: Airport Public Safety Zones guidance
official_sources.fact: DfT guidance defines Public Safety Zones near runway ends and a general presumption against development that increases people living, working or congregating within them.
official_sources.gate: PSZ policy applies only where the exact current PSZ map covers the site and does not replace a planning decision.

official_sources.name: MOD wind farms safeguarding
official_sources.fact: MOD safeguarding covers aerodromes, explosive stores, radar, communications, ranges and other defence interests potentially affected by development including wind turbines.
official_sources.gate: MOD consultation or potential impact is not proof of objection, refusal or unmitigable conflict on a specific site.

official_sources.name: HSE role in land use planning
official_sources.fact: HSE states it is a statutory consultee for planning applications around major hazard sites and major accident hazard pipelines and sets consultation distances.
official_sources.gate: A consultation distance is a trigger for HSE advice, not an automatic planning prohibition.

official_sources.name: Why HSE is involved
official_sources.fact: HSE explains land-use planning controls around major hazard establishments and pipelines and its advisory role in planning decisions.
official_sources.gate: HSE advice is material safety advice; it is not itself the planning permission decision.

official_sources.name: HSE Planning Advice Web App
official_sources.fact: HSE's Web App uses inner, middle and outer consultation zones plus development type, size and intensity to provide advice.
official_sources.gate: A Web App zone or generic result must not be treated as exact consent status, hazardous-substances consent or explosives-site advice.

official_sources.name: HSE developers planning advice
official_sources.fact: HSE offers consultation-zone checks and pre-application advice for developments near major hazard sites and major accident hazard pipelines.
official_sources.gate: Pre-application advice does not guarantee planning approval and may not cover explosives or nuclear-site consultation routes.

official_sources.name: HSE land-use planning methodology
official_sources.fact: HSE methodology explains consultation zones, sensitivity levels, multiple hazards, hazardous-substances consent, pipelines and explosives-site exceptions.
official_sources.gate: Methodology must be applied using exact proposal and hazard data; it is not a parcel score or generic buffer rule.

official_sources.name: HSE land-use planning resources
official_sources.fact: HSE provides official user guides and resources for planning authorities and developers using its land-use planning advice system.
official_sources.gate: Resource availability is not evidence of site coverage or a particular HSE advice outcome.

official_sources.name: HSE land-use planning background
official_sources.fact: HSE explains the history and current framework for land-use planning advice around hazardous installations and pipelines.
official_sources.gate: Background methodology does not establish a live hazard, consultation zone or planning constraint for a parcel.

official_sources.name: HSE hazardous substances consent
official_sources.fact: HSE states hazardous substances consent is required at defined controlled quantities, with HSE consulted and three risk zones produced where consent is granted.
official_sources.gate: Need for consent or HSE risk zones does not prove consent exists, remains live or covers an exact parcel without the authoritative consent and plan.

official_sources.name: GOV.UK hazardous substances guidance
official_sources.fact: Government planning guidance covers hazardous substances consent applications, consultation, modification, revocation, continuation and public participation.
official_sources.gate: Hazardous-substances planning guidance is not evidence of an individual site's live consent, quantities, conditions or consultation distance.

official_sources.name: HSC Smart Forms FAQ
official_sources.fact: HSE's Smart Forms FAQ supports new consent, condition variation and continuation applications and describes required site/substance information.
official_sources.gate: A generated form or submitted application is not granted consent or proof of acceptable residual risk.

official_sources.name: HSC Smart Forms application
official_sources.fact: HSE provides a Smart Forms tool to prepare hazardous substances consent application documents for submission to the local authority.
official_sources.gate: Form preparation does not validate, determine or grant hazardous substances consent.

official_sources.name: HSE call-in policy
official_sources.fact: HSE describes factors used when a planning authority proposes to grant permission against HSE safety advice near major hazard sites or pipelines.
official_sources.gate: Potential call-in or an Advise Against position is not a final Secretary of State or planning-authority decision.

official_sources.name: COMAH Regulations 2015 overview
official_sources.fact: HSE explains COMAH 2015 major-hazard duties and notes land-use planning requirements are implemented through separate planning legislation.
official_sources.gate: COMAH operator status or compliance does not equal hazardous-substances consent or planning permission.

official_sources.name: MAH pipeline notification
official_sources.fact: HSE explains statutory notifications for major accident hazard pipelines before construction, use, operator changes and major modifications.
official_sources.gate: Pipeline notification is not planning permission, route acquisition, construction completion or evidence that a parcel lies in a consultation zone.

official_sources.name: HSE pipelines FAQs
official_sources.fact: HSE describes three land-use-planning zones for notified major accident hazard pipelines derived from quantified risk assessment.
official_sources.gate: Generic pipeline zones or risk methodology require exact notified pipeline geometry and zone distances before parcel conclusions.

official_sources.name: HSE RR1186 pipeline failure rates
official_sources.fact: HSE research supports quantified-risk assessment inputs for major accident hazard pipeline land-use planning.
official_sources.gate: Research failure rates are methodology evidence, not proof of a pipeline's location, condition or exact parcel risk.

official_sources.name: HSE pipeline standards
official_sources.fact: HSE describes current good-practice expectations for pipeline design, operation and maintenance under the Pipelines Safety Regulations.
official_sources.gate: Compliance standards are not a planning consent, consultation-zone result or exact-site development clearance.

official_sources.name: Explosives safeguarding plans
official_sources.fact: HSE states licensed explosives sites must submit safeguarding plans showing licensed-site extent and separation-distance envelopes.
official_sources.gate: A safeguarding plan requires the exact current licence and distances; a generic explosives-site signal is not parcel-level prohibition.

official_sources.name: Explosives local authority assent
official_sources.fact: HSE explains local-authority assent for certain explosives licences and distinguishes safety assent from planning appropriateness.
official_sources.gate: Local-authority assent or refusal is not planning permission and must not be conflated with planning merits.

official_sources.name: Explosives safety requirements
official_sources.fact: HSE explains separation-distance requirements and that development within separation zones can affect permitted explosives quantities.
official_sources.gate: Separation distances depend on the exact licence, hazard type, quantity and building context; generic buffers must not be invented.

official_sources.name: Applying for explosives licence
official_sources.fact: HSE guidance distinguishes licensing authority and route according to activity, quantity, location and ability to meet separation distances.
official_sources.gate: Application route or licence eligibility is not a granted licence, current safeguarding plan or planning permission.

official_sources.name: Explosives FAQ
official_sources.fact: HSE FAQ explains safeguarding plans and that separation distances depend on explosive type, quantity and building type, with defined exceptions.
official_sources.gate: A stored quantity or historic licence alone does not establish current separation-distance geometry without authoritative live licence evidence.

official_sources.name: Planning Data safeguarded aerodrome
official_sources.fact: Planning Data currently reports zero safeguarded-aerodrome records, zero providers and no collection attempt.
official_sources.gate: Zero platform data means NO_DATA and must not be interpreted as absence of safeguarded aerodromes or consultation requirements.

official_sources.name: Planning Data safeguarded military explosives site
official_sources.fact: Planning Data currently reports zero safeguarded-military-explosives-site records, zero providers and no collection attempt.
official_sources.gate: Zero platform data means NO_DATA and must not be interpreted as absence of military explosives safeguarding.
